about: Source list for the Research tab of the Scholar Compass tour. The product sheet (content/atlas/part-compass.json, family research field, line 14) says: 'Designed from O*NET occupation data and its Interest Profiler. Each covered career's entry requirements carry a named source.' The owner pasted a ten-topic list (below). Every external source was opened on 27 Nov 2026 on its publisher or owner site and described only as far as that page says. onetcenter.org, onetonline.org, services.onetcenter.org and ncda.org were read with a plain command-line request (and the O*NET pages also with the fetch tool); the two regulator PDFs were downloaded and read as text. No figure is taken from any source. Topics are themes: where the repo names no theory behind a topic, the entry says so and no outside page was researched. Repo evidence paths are relative to C:\Users\MILAN\Downloads and were read in source on the same date. Code searched: next_lms_erp (app, config, routes, docs, database/neo4j incl. cai and frameworks), lms_k12 (app, lib, docs), hp_erp (app, config, Docs), and g2gv0 only for the product sheet. A whole-repo search (vendor and node_modules left out) found no Savickas, Bandura, Lent-Brown-Hackett or SCCT, Krumboltz, Gottfredson, Donald Super or 'career adaptability' in next_lms_erp, lms_k12 or hp_erp. The only Big Five mention is the words 'IPIP Big Five' in one hp_erp sales-catalogue row (config/portfolio_seed_data.json:606, readiness 'In development', not confirmed) with no implementation in next_lms_erp or lms_k12. 'Self-efficacy' appears in next_lms_erp only for learning reflection. 'Internship' appears in the Alumni and recruitment modules and in one static report line, not in any Compass screen. The ten product feature names from the owner's list were also searched by name in next_lms_erp, lms_k12, hp_erp and g2gv0 (app, config, docs, lib, components, database, routes): none found.
supplied_by_owner: Career Development Theory: how career interests and identity develop over time -> Longitudinal career profile
Interest Assessment: what activities and occupational areas attract students -> Interest intelligence
Aptitude and Ability: what abilities students demonstrate or are developing -> Strength and aptitude profile
Personality and Work Preferences: how students prefer to work and interact -> Career environment matching
Career Self-Efficacy: how confident students are in performing career-related tasks -> Confidence and readiness
Career Decision-Making: how students compare options and make informed choices -> Career decision support
Career Awareness: how students discover occupations and industries -> Career exploration
Career Adaptability: how students prepare for changing careers and environments -> Future-readiness intelligence
Skills and Occupation Mapping: which skills, qualifications and competencies are required for occupations -> Career-Skill Knowledge Graph
Experiential Career Learning: how projects, internships and real-world exposure influence career interests -> Prayogshala and career projects

sources.name: O*NET Interest Profiler (O*NET Resource Center, U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration)
sources.page_title: Interest Profiler (IP) at O*NET Resource Center
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA); developed by the National Center for O*NET Development
sources.what_the_pages_say: The page calls the O*NET Interest Profiler a family of self-assessment career exploration tools that help people discover the type of work activities and occupations they would like. It measures six types of occupational interests: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, Conventional. It lists a 30-question Mini-IP and a 60-question IP Short Form, and the feature line 'Compatible with Holland's R-I-A-S-E-C Interest Structure (Holland, 1985)'. The IP Manual page (March 2021) says it is a vocational interest inventory designed for use in educational planning, career exploration and career guidance, and that 'John Holland's (1997) RIASEC theoretical model' is the basis of the Interest Profiler scales. Page footer: site updated October 6, 2026.
sources.licence_or_terms: "The O*NET Interest Profiler may be redistributed or used to develop other assessments under a choice of licenses." and "Interest Profiler (IP) by U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License." (https://www.onetcenter.org/IP.html). The Career Exploration Tools licence page (https://www.onetcenter.org/license_tools.html) offers two options: CC BY-ND 4.0 to copy without modification, or the O*NET Tools Developer License to modify, edit or extend, which asks users to credit the source, link to the licence and "validate all products incorporating content from the Tools". It also says: "O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA", "The trademark symbol must be properly displayed when referring to O*NET" and, for modified content, "USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications."
sources.how_the_slide_uses_it: States only what the source is. It does not say Scholar Compass conforms to it or is endorsed by it.

sources.name: The O*NET Content Model (O*NET Resource Center)
sources.page_title: The O*NET Content Model at O*NET Resource Center
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, via the O*NET Resource Center
sources.what_the_pages_say: The page says the Content Model is the foundation of O*NET and organizes the most important information about jobs and workers into a clear, structured system, and that it 'is based on research about jobs and how people work'. It names six main areas (Worker Characteristics, Worker Requirements, Experience Requirements, Occupational Requirements, Occupation-Specific Info, Workforce Characteristics). Under Worker Characteristics the outline lists Career Interests, Abilities and Work Styles; under Worker Requirements it lists Skills, Knowledge and Education. LIMIT: the current outline does not list Work Values, although the product code reads work-values tables (see owner_to_confirm).
sources.licence_or_terms: The page itself shows no licence line and no date (only a 'License agreements' link in its menu). The database licence page (https://www.onetcenter.org/license_db.html, titled 'O*NET 31.0 Database Content License') says: "the content of the O*NET 31.0 Database is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" and asks users to "credit the O*NET 31.0 Database and the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration as the original source, link to the license, and indicate where any changes were made to the original."

sources.name: National Career Development Guidelines (NCDG), National Career Development Association
sources.page_title: NCDG Website (home); NCDA | The Framework; NCDA | History of NCDG
sources.what_the_pages_say: The NCDG are 'a framework of career development competencies and indicators of mastery, including a recommended strategy for implementing career development programs for youth or adults.' The pages describe a 2024 version with three domains: Career Development (defined as meeting career goals through information management and decision-making, while mastering employability skills and integrating world conditions), Academic and Lifelong Learning, and Social Emotional Learning. Indicators are presented in three learning stages derived from Bloom's Taxonomy (knowledge acquisition, application, reflection), 'not tied to an individual's age or level of education'. First released by the National Occupational Information Coordinating Committee in 1989 and handed to NCDA in 2007 to maintain. One indicator example on the home page (CD1.K4) lists self-efficacy and flexibility among career management traits; the repo does not implement that indicator.
sources.licence_note: No reuse licence is stated on the three pages read. Footer shows '2026 National Career Development Guidelines' with links to Contact Us, Legal Disclaimer and Privacy Policy; the Legal Disclaimer page was not opened.
sources.how_the_slide_uses_it: States only what the source is. It does not say Scholar Compass conforms to it or is endorsed by it.
sources.compass_note: No NCDG mention exists in the four Compass screens folders, CareerIntelligence services or counselling controllers (searched), and part-compass.json does not name it. The only link to Compass is that ncdg.cypher maps NCDG goals onto the same Occupation, Exam and Degree nodes the alignment check uses.

proposed_rows.text: The O*NET® Content Model organizes information about jobs and workers, from interests, abilities and work styles to the skills and knowledge needed.
proposed_rows.source: O*NET Resource Center, The O*NET Content Model, onetcenter.org

proposed_rows.text: O*NET® OnLine, sponsored by the U.S. Department of Labor, is a career exploration and job analysis tool describing the world of work.
proposed_rows.source: O*NET OnLine, onetonline.org, U.S. Department of Labor

proposed_rows.text: The National Career Development Guidelines are a framework of career development competencies and indicators of mastery, maintained by the National Career Development Association.
proposed_rows.source: National Career Development Association, NCDG, ncda.org

proposed_rows.text: Council of Architecture is a statutory authority whose regulations set minimum standards of architectural education, including admission conditions.
proposed_rows.source: Council of Architecture, Minimum Standards of Architectural Education Regulations, 2020

Career-Skill Knowledge Graph (feature name; the repo says 'career knowledge graph')
Prayogshala and career projects (Prayogshala exists as a curriculum lab with no career link; career projects: none)
Career Development Theory: no named theory (no Super, Savickas)
Aptitude and Ability: no named aptitude source

Career Adaptability: no repo evidence at all

owner_to_confirm: NO CODE EVIDENCE, so the slide must not claim them: the ten feature names in no_code_cites, and any theory behind Career Development, Aptitude, Personality, Self-Efficacy, Decision-Making, Adaptability and Experiential Career Learning. Only Interest Assessment (O*NET Interest Profiler, Holland RIASEC), Career Awareness data (O*NET) and Skills and Occupation Mapping (O*NET, named entry-requirement sources) have a named source in the repo.

Wording on the sheet: part-compass.json:116 says 'Designed from the O*NET Interest Profiler'. The code fetches the Interest Profiler questions and results from O*NET Web Services and passes them through unchanged (types.ts:5; lmsCounsellingController.php:1174 and :1208). 'Uses the O*NET Interest Profiler through O*NET Web Services' is what the code supports. The sheet's other lead, 'Designed from O*NET occupation data', rests on locally stored onet_* tables and the O*NET codes in the career graph.

O*NET credit and registration: the Web Services terms ask for a link to the O*NET Web Services site near the use of the information and for the site to be registered. Searching the four K12 career folders for O*NET found 6 matches, all code comments (types.ts, KnowingYourselfHub.tsx, career-intelligence api.ts and MentorSuggestions.tsx), so no on-screen credit was found. Registration of the production site was not checked (credential variable names ONET_USERNAME and ONET_PASSWORD exist at .env.example:22; values not read).

O*NET naming and endorsement: the licence pages require the trademark symbol, O*NET used as an adjective, and say USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed or tested modified content. The slide wording should follow that and must not imply O*NET endorses or has assessed Scholar Compass.

Holland year mismatch: the O*NET Interest Profiler page says Holland, 1985; the IP Manual and the repo text (lmsCounsellingController.php:709) say Holland (1997). The slide names Holland and RIASEC without a year. Holland's own book was not opened.

O*NET data version: the Content Model page opened lists Career Interests, Abilities and Work Styles under Worker Characteristics and no Work Values, but the code reads work-values tables (lmsCounsellingController.php:478, :713) and the explorer menu has an 'Interests & Work Values' group (EduSideMenu.tsx:17). The O*NET database version loaded into onet_* tables is not recorded in the repo (the licence page names version 31.0 as current). Keep work values off the slide.

Career Awareness name clash: the owner's topic 'Career Awareness: how students discover occupations and industries' is what the Career Explorer sub-module does. The K12 sub-module named Career Awareness is certainty, ambition, alignment and originality, and its text cites no source. Decide which one the research row belongs to.

NCDG on Compass: neither part-compass.json nor any Compass screen or service names NCDG. The repo links it only through ncdg.cypher (goals mapped onto the career-graph Occupation, Exam and Degree nodes) and PAL config. Include row 4 only if the owner accepts that link; otherwise drop it. Version note: the code uses the earlier domain names and codes (PS, EDL, CM) and a goal count of 8 (ncdg.cypher:75) while the NCDA pages read now show the 2024 domains and 'eleven goals'; the slide names NCDG and the National Career Development Guidelines only, no version.

Entry-requirement sources: of the 11 covered careers only Architect (Council of Architecture, opened) and Veterinarian (Veterinary Council of India, first pages read) cite a regulator. The others cite education portals or blogs (careers360, sartha.in, crescent.education, clatnlti.com), so 'named source' is true but 'official source' is not. The veterinary cypher comment calls its document a circular; the file opened is an information bulletin for online counselling, academic year 2026-27. The Council of Architecture file is a gazette notification dated 11 Aug 2020; an architecture degree also needs an aptitude test under regulation 4.

Interest results do not feed career evidence or the alignment check, and nothing is saved (CareerCounsellingNarrator.php:17-22; sheet owner_to_confirm). The slide must not say the Interest Profiler informs guidance, alignment or recommendations.

IPIP Big Five: named for the Career Intelligence & Counselling offer (SCH-04) in hp_erp/config/portfolio_seed_data.json:606, a sales-catalogue row with readiness 'In development' and readiness_confirmed false, together with 'KASBA + NCDG competency framework'. No code in next_lms_erp or lms_k12 implements it, and KASBA in the product is a staff and organisation capability model (part-insight.json:284 says not to link it to students). If the owner's Personality and Work Preferences topic comes from that row, the slide must not claim it. The IPIP page was opened and is recorded above, but no row is proposed.

Internships and real-world exposure: the product has alumni-posted jobs, internships, apprenticeships and projects that students see (Alumni module), but they are not part of Compass and not tied to careers counselling. If the owner wants Experiential Career Learning on the Compass slide, that is a link to build or confirm, not one the code shows.

Terms in the repo that are outside the owner's list: Gardner's multiple intelligences (gardner.cypher:2, PAL signal pal_architecture.php:830) and MBTI (CounsellingCourses.tsx:17, a school-set card; test licensing is already an open item on the sheet). Not researched and not proposed as rows.
Words to keep off the slide: the PAL Career pathway tagline uses 'validated' (pal_architecture.php:780); the Career Awareness text asserts links to earnings and satisfaction with no source.

Not opened: Holland's own book and any publisher page for it; the NCDA Legal Disclaimer page; the full eligibility text of the Veterinary Council bulletin. No page was skipped for a fetch error: all pages above opened.
